tool_arguments.query: AMD Data Center segment revenue Q3 2026

events.content: AMD Data Center segment revenue Q3 2026

AMD has **not yet reported Q3 2026 results** as of October 17, 2026, so no actual Q3 Data Center segment-revenue figure—or disclosed Q3 split between Instinct GPUs and EPYC CPUs—is available. 

For Q3 2026, AMD’s guidance is for **total company revenue of approximately $13.0 billion, plus or minus $0.3 billion**; it did not provide Data Center segment guidance in that release. [[1]] 

The latest reported segment result is **Q2 2026 Data Center revenue of $6.7 billion**, up **107% year over year**, driven by strong demand for **AMD EPYC processors** and **AMD Instinct GPUs**. [[1]] 

Management said it expected Data Center sales to **accelerate in the second half of 2026**, citing accelerating EPYC demand, scaling Instinct deployments, and the beginning of the Helios ramp. [[1]]

tool_arguments.query: AMD Q2 2026 earnings call transcript Instinct GPU Data Center revenue split

events.content: AMD Q2 2026 earnings call transcript Instinct GPU Data Center revenue split

AMD did not disclose a dollar revenue split between Instinct accelerators and EPYC server CPUs for Q2 2026; it reported them together within its Data Center segment. [[1]] 

Data Center revenue was **$6.718 billion** in Q2 2026, up **107% year over year**, with AMD attributing the performance to strong demand for both EPYC processors and Instinct GPUs. [[1]] 

The available qualitative detail is that EPYC sales increased by **more than 70% year over year**, while Instinct sales **more than doubled year over year**, but neither figure was quantified in dollars; therefore, an Instinct-versus-EPYC revenue allocation cannot be reliably calculated from AMD’s reported results. [[2]]

tool_arguments.query: AMD embedded segment revenue Q2 2026 Xilinx FPGA

events.content: AMD embedded segment revenue Q2 2026 Xilinx FPGA

AMD’s Embedded segment generated **$977 million of revenue in Q2 2026**, up **19% year over year** from **$824 million in Q2 2025** and up from **$873 million in Q1 2026**. AMD attributed the growth to strengthening demand across multiple end markets; the segment includes the company’s Xilinx-derived adaptive-computing/FPGA portfolio, although AMD did not separately disclose Xilinx FPGA-only revenue. [[1]]

Related coverage:
AMD does not separately disclose **Xilinx FPGA revenue**; it reports the broader **Embedded** segment, which includes embedded CPUs, GPUs, APUs, FPGAs, systems-on-modules, and Adaptive SoC products. [[1]] 

For FY2025 (year ended December 27, 2025), AMD Embedded revenue was **$3.454 billion**, down **3%** from **$3.557 billion** in FY2024, with AMD attributing the decline to mixed demand in certain end markets. [[2]] 

Embedded operating income was **$1.243 billion** in FY2025, versus **$1.421 billion** in FY2024. [[2]] 

For historical context, Embedded revenue was **$5.321 billion in FY2023**, then fell to **$3.557 billion in FY2024**, principally as customers normalized inventory; the FY2023 Embedded revenue increase had been driven primarily by inclusion of Xilinx embedded-product revenue. [[3]] [[4]] 

The latest quarterly figure in the retrieved AMD disclosures is **$857 million in Q3 2025**, down **8% year over year**. [[5]]
